metadata.title: Second-pass adjudication of all 27 prospective primary-reader candidates
metadata.scope: Current-text adjudication after the entire prospective pass was frozen, informed by the complete RR9 audit. This is simulated reader reasoning, not human observation or independent revalidation of every theorem.

status_meanings.retain: A specific current concern remains; see bounded recommendation.
status_meanings.retain_reframed: Some initial wording was too broad; only the explicitly narrowed current concern survives.
status_meanings.resolved: The requested bridge is already supplied by current material and no finding remains.
status_meanings.discard: A current defect is not established.
status_meanings.discard_false_positive: A concrete initial suspicion is disproved by current source.
status_meanings.optional: Potential improvement, not an established defect or required repair.
status_meanings.merge_optional: Do not count separately; an optional observation is covered by the named candidate.

critical_corrections: FP-018: the early three-property ingredient preview exists; withdraw the claim that a usable interface arrives only at 3.17.
FP-026: section 3.18 exists and its catalogue destination is valid.
metadata.finding_limits: Only five candidates are eligible, three overlapping RR9 survivors. No candidate alleges a false mathematical theorem. Optional and discarded rows must not be promoted as new findings.

candidates.title: Shorten the opening probability argument to its mechanism
candidates.reason: The opening already gives a useful column/winner explanation, so the problem is not complete absence of an object. It then asks a first-time reader to retain L, the fixed-time joint event, r=20 log m, a union over query times and heavy-column accounting before a worked board or simulator exists. Later sections justify all of this; the surviving issue is the amount of technical state required by the synopsis.
candidates.recommendation: Keep the planted-zero/cell dichotomy and mL versus square-root-m exponent comparison in the synopsis; place the fixed-time event and numerical choice with the first lower-bound roadmap. Preserve the exact proof in section 6.
candidates.prospective_observation: The opening synopsis introduces the numeric r=20 log2 m, allowance L, a fixed-time joint event, heavy columns and the union bound before a column/address example exists. The broad mechanism is understandable, but the precise event is an opaque miniature proof. Consider moving the fixed-time event and coefficients to a first-proof map while retaining the mL versus sqrt(m) synopsis.

One early sentence contrasting the two tasks could help an outsider, but the synopsis need not prove certification in place. This is an optional first-encounter bridge, not a mathematical gap.

candidates.prospective_observation: 'A circuit transcript in the cell certifies the values' first asks an outsider to accept a cheap certification of a classically hard function. A short bridge should distinguish querying a supplied transcript from computing it and flag the one-sided definition that makes the certification possible.

The explanation is precise but the reader must remember that Lemma4.1 belongs to §6.1 and bare equations to another paper; add role names at subsequent lemma citations or adopt local named labels consistently.

candidates.title: Expose the accounting behind the asserted exact circuit size
candidates.reason: The source provides primitive arithmetic costs and the butterfly count, then asserts an exact composite S identity. The non-transform bracket terms and final +7 are not assigned to constructors. The later coarse inequality is shown, so this is a reconstructibility gap in an asserted exact count, not proof that the count or final bound is false.
candidates.recommendation: Add a short summand-to-constructor ledger, or explicitly limit the claim to an upper bound with a shown derivation if exact equality is unnecessary. Include the constant gates and the final +7.
candidates.prospective_observation: The exact S identity is introduced as a recovered constructor count, but the reader receives only one large expression. A small accounting table assigning each summand to transforms, sign layers, final sum and comparisons would make the claimed equality reconstructible without source archaeology.

The stated jobs explain why boundedness and integration by parts matter, but not why choosing Psi=1/(2sqrt(2+x²)) produces the useful phi. A short design line deriving phi=xPsi−Psi prime from the chosen kernel would improve reconstructibility without adding a theorem.

candidates.title: Let the complete reading route reach the total construction before the long hardness engine
candidates.reason: Correction to the frozen first impression: a usable three-property preview already exists at lines 454–460, so it is false to say that the interface first appears only at 3.17. The remaining chronological burden is real: after that preview, the complete reader traverses the full independent analytic hardness derivation before the addressed function and its first complete board. The skip route helps selective readers but does not change publication order.
candidates.recommendation: Consider using the existing three-property preview as the explicit contract, then present the addressed construction and both proof branches, and place the complete hardness derivation as a later proof module. Keep the locally proved uniform bound available before any growing-k conclusion; do not replace it by an unverified external assumption.
candidates.correction_of_prospective_observation: The claim of a missing early usable ingredient interface is withdrawn; only the global sequencing proposal survives.
candidates.prospective_observation: The complete chronological reader reaches the usable three-property interface only after roughly1,200 source lines of Forrelation development, before any complete addressed board. A two-part architecture could introduce the §3.17 contract early, complete §§4–7, and then rebuild the analytic hardness engine. This preserves a complete proof while making every technical lemma answer a previously encountered need. The current route instructions permit skipping, but do not repair the publication-order burden.

Each distinction is careful, but their cumulative placement interrupts the algorithmic arc.
